title: Valle d'Itria & Salento by Bike

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — 36°C inland, zero shade on the murgia, and coastal roads jammed with beach traffic

accommodation.note: Trullo and albergo diffuso €80–€130 pppn; a Savelletri masseria doubles it

food.note: Fornello pronto grills €15–€22; Lecce trattorie €25–€35 with wine

transport.note: Airport transfers, one FSE regional train leg, luggage move to Lecce

activities.note: Road or gravel hire €190–€240/week, Egnazia €7, Torre Guaceto guided entry €10

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5 — rolling rather than mountainous, but 700–1,100 m of ascent a day accumulates on rough limestone lanes

gatewayAirport: BRI Bari Karol Wojtyła, 65 min to Locorotondo; BDS Brindisi Salento is 45 min to Ostuni and 40 min to Lecce
summary: The Valle d'Itria is a shallow limestone basin stitched with dry-stone walls, olive trunks the width of a car, and trulli that appear in fields the way boulders do elsewhere. Riding it means constant micro-climbs on white lanes between Locorotondo, Cisternino and Martina Franca, then a fast drop off the Murgia escarpment at Ostuni to a coastline of dune, macchia and Roman ruin. The last two days shift south to the Salento, where the landscape flattens, the light hardens, and the ride from Lecce to Otranto runs through baroque towns and scarred olive groves. It is a cycling week built around food and surface variety rather than climbing, and it rewards a gravel bike over a race bike.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Locorotondo, the valley's first white lanes
itinerary.morning: Land at Bari, transfer to Locorotondo and collect the bike from Puglia On Bike. Walk the circular centro storico — the town is a perfect ring of whitewashed houses with pitched cummerse roofs found nowhere else in Puglia.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride a soft opener anti-clockwise through Contrada Serralta and Contrada Trito on strade bianche, looping past working trulli and vineyards of verdeca and bianco d'Alessano.
itinerary.evening: Quanto Basta on Via Morelli in Locorotondo — craft beer, bruschetta and a terrace over the valley. Follow with a nightcap at U Curdunn.
itinerary.dayStats: 31 km / 380 m ascent / 45% paved, 55% strade bianche

itinerary.title: The Trulli Ring, and Alberobello before the buses
itinerary.morning: Leave by 07:30 for Alberobello so you reach the Rione Monti and Rione Aia Piccola trullo districts before the coach parties. Ride the back lanes via Contrada Sisto rather than the SP113.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Martina Franca for the baroque Palazzo Ducale and Via Cavour, then Cisternino on the ridge lanes. This is the loop's rough section — expect washboard limestone.
itinerary.evening: Cisternino's fornello pronto ritual: choose your meat at a butcher such as Zio Pietro, they grill it, you eat it upstairs with a jug of local red. Bombette are the obligatory order.
itinerary.dayStats: 68 km / 890 m ascent / 40% paved, 60% strade bianche and farm track

itinerary.title: Murgia plateau, Selva di Fasano and the escarpment view
itinerary.morning: Climb east from Locorotondo through Selva di Fasano to the plateau lip at 431 m, where the land falls 400 m to the Adriatic in a single step. The Montevicoli ramp hits 11%.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend to Ceglie Messapica for the Messapian walls and a long lunch, then return by the Contrada Vitti white roads. Ceglie is the valley's serious food town and worth the detour on its own.
itinerary.evening: Back in Locorotondo, dinner at La Taverna del Duca on Via Papatotero — orecchiette with cime di rapa, and a bottle of Locorotondo DOC white.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km / 1,050 m ascent / 60% paved, 40% white road / high point 431 m / max gradient 11%

itinerary.title: Off the escarpment to Ostuni and the coast
itinerary.morning: Ride the descent to Ostuni via Contrada Lamacoppa, then climb the last kilometre through Porta San Demetrio into the white city. Coffee in Piazza della Libertà, then the cathedral's rose window.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop to the coast through the ancient olive groves of the Piana degli Olivi Secolari — trees dated at over a thousand years, several fenced as monumental. Reach the Torre Guaceto marine reserve and ride its sand-and-hardpack coast track.
itinerary.evening: Osteria del Tempo Perso in Ostuni, cut into the rock behind the cathedral. Order the lamb and a Susumaniello.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km / 780 m ascent / 65% paved, 32% hardpack, 3% dune sand / Ostuni climb 8.1 km at 3.2%, max 9%

itinerary.title: Egnazia, Savelletri and the transfer to Lecce
itinerary.morning: North along the coast road past Torre Canne to the Parco Archeologico di Egnazia, a Messapian and Roman port town with a preserved Via Traiana paving slab and a small but excellent museum.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch at Savelletri on the harbour, then either ride inland to Fasano and take the regional train, or transfer by van to Lecce with the bikes. Arrive in time to walk Piazza del Duomo at dusk.
itinerary.evening: Alle Due Corti on Corte dei Giugni in Lecce for uncompromising Salentine cooking — ciceri e tria, and pezzetti di cavallo if you are curious.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km ridden / 520 m ascent / 85% paved / Egnazia entry €7 / transfer to Lecce 1 h 15 min

itinerary.title: Lecce to Otranto and the Adriatic edge
itinerary.morning: Out of Lecce on the SP1 toward Vernole and Acaya, a fortified Renaissance village with intact walls, then the Le Cesine WWF reserve where the road runs between lagoon and dune.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue via San Foca and Roca Vecchia to Otranto. The Grotta della Poesia sinkhole at Roca is the swim stop. In Otranto, the cathedral's twelfth-century mosaic floor and the martyrs' chapel are 20 minutes well spent.
itinerary.evening: Peccato di Vino on Via Rondachi in Otranto — raw seafood and Negroamaro on a lane behind the castle.
itinerary.dayStats: 79 km / 610 m ascent / 90% paved, 10% dune track / total climbing below 200 m altitude throughout
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Rollo, Lecce (train back from Otranto, or van shuttle)

itinerary.title: Salento loop through Galatina and out
itinerary.morning: A final flat loop south-west from Lecce to Galatina for the Basilica di Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, whose frescoed interior is the best painted surface in Puglia and almost always empty.
itinerary.afternoon: Return via Copertino's Angevin castle and the vineyards around Leverano. Hand the bike to the operator's Lecce drop-off point, agreed at booking.
itinerary.evening: Pasticciotto and caffè leccese at Avio in Lecce before the transfer to Brindisi.
itinerary.dayStats: 66 km / 340 m ascent / 95% paved / one-way drop-off fee €50–€80
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Rollo, Lecce, or a Brindisi airport hotel

accommodationStrategy.name: Sotto le Cummerse
accommodationStrategy.description: Restored houses scattered through the historic centre, all with kitchens, and a ground-floor annexe used for bike storage. You wake up inside the walled town and are on white roads within 400 m. Roughly €95–€135 double, and the reception will handle Puglia On Bike deliveries.

accommodationStrategy.name: Masseria Il Frantoio
accommodationStrategy.description: A seventeenth-century masseria with a subterranean olive mill that doubles as bike storage. Positioned on the SS16 side of Ostuni, so you exit straight onto the coastal lanes. Eight-course estate dinners on request; €180–€260 double, and worth exactly one night.

accommodationStrategy.name: Palazzo Rollo
accommodationStrategy.description: A seventeenth-century palazzo on Corte dei Rollo, inside the pedestrian core but with an internal courtyard for bikes and a rooftop loggia. Two minutes from Piazza Sant'Oronzo and about €90–€140 double, which is the sweet spot for two nights of Salento riding.

logistics.connectivity: 4G and 5G are strong throughout, including on the white roads. Italy is in the EU so roaming is included. Offline mapping still matters: many strade bianche are unnamed and Google routing will occasionally send you into a private masseria drive.
logistics.emergency: 112 across Italy; 118 still reaches ambulance dispatch directly. The main trauma centres are Ospedale Perrino in Brindisi and Vito Fazzi in Lecce. Italy requires cyclists to carry a reflective gilet and use lights in tunnels and after dusk on extra-urban roads.
logistics.weather: Spring brings the scirocco, a hot southerly carrying Saharan dust that drops visibility and coats bikes in red grit. Autumn produces short, violent coastal thunderstorms. Wind, not gradient, is the limiting factor on the Salento coast — 25–35 km/h afternoon sea breezes are routine.
logistics.bookingWindows: Masserie around Savelletri and Ostuni sell out for May and September six months ahead. Rental bikes need four to six weeks. Alle Due Corti and Osteria del Tempo Perso take same-week bookings outside August. Torre Guaceto's guided reserve entries should be reserved a few days out.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal, but the butcher-grills of Cisternino and rural masseria farm shops often prefer cash. A coperto of €2–€3 per person is standard and is not a tip; tipping beyond rounding up is not expected.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Italy; motorway tolls apply on the A14 north of Bari only. Trenitalia regional bike tickets are €3.50 for 24 hours. FSE regional trains take bikes with a supplement but have very limited space, no reservation, and none on replacement buses. Rental cars crossing to Albania by ferry from Brindisi need written permission.
logistics.permits: Torre Guaceto is a protected marine and terrestrial reserve — stay on marked tracks, no off-piste riding on dunes, and swimming is zoned. Egnazia archaeological park charges €7. Drone flying is banned over archaeological sites and requires ENAC-compliant registration. Monumental olive trees are legally protected; do not lean bikes against them.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable but heavily chlorinated and tastes of it; most riders buy still water. Xylella fastidiosa has killed vast tracts of Salento olives — the dead groves are not fire-safe, and cigarette discipline matters. Jellyfish blooms of Pelagia noctiluca hit the Adriatic coast in late summer. Loose dogs on farm lanes are a genuine hazard; do not sprint.

proTips: Reach Alberobello's Rione Monti before 08:30 or after 18:30. Between those hours it is the single most crowded square kilometre in southern Italy.
Ride the white roads clockwise out of Locorotondo — the dry-stone walls throw shade on the eastern side of the lanes until about 11:00, which is worth several degrees in May.
In Cisternino, order at the butcher counter and pay there, not at the table. Tell them how many bombette per person; four is a normal serving, six is a cyclist's.
Ask your masseria for a 07:00 breakfast the night before. Puglian hotels default to 08:30, which is an hour of lost cool riding.
Torre Guaceto's inner tracks are sand over hardpack. Drop 10 psi at the gate and re-inflate at the exit; the reserve office has no pump.
Buy Locorotondo DOC and Valle d'Itria whites at the source rather than in Ostuni — the same bottle is routinely 40% cheaper in the producing village.
FSE track works regularly suspend the Martina Franca line at short notice. Confirm the day before, and always have a van fallback for the Lecce transfer.
The Grotta della Poesia at Roca Vecchia is free and unstaffed early; by noon in shoulder season it has a queue for the single entry ladder.

raw.Signature loop — the Trulli Ring (Locoro: 68 km, 890 m ascent, run entirely on strade bianche and single-track asphalt lanes between dry-stone walls, with no climb over 3 km.
raw.Escarpment climb — Ostuni from Villanova: 8.1 km, 260 m ascent, 3.2% average with a 9% pinch through the Porta San Demetrio approach, summit 218 m. Short, but it is the only sustained gradient on the coast side.
raw.Martina Franca–Ceglie Messapica murgia c: 4.6 km at 4.8%, maximum 11% on the Contrada Montevicoli ramp, high point 431 m near Selva di Fasano — the top of the plateau and the day's only real view.
raw.Week surface split: roughly 55% paved (much of it patched, chip-sealed provincial lane), 30% strade bianche and compacted limestone farm track, 12% cracked concrete masseria access roads, 3% sandy dune track inside Torre Guaceto. Puglian asphalt is often worse than the gravel — run 35–40 mm.
raw.Bike hire: Puglia On Bike, based in Locorotondo, is the region's most established rental and guiding outfit, with road, gravel and e-bike fleets and delivery across the Valle d'Itria. Velo Service and Veloce Rental both operate road and gravel hire out of Alberobello, and CCT Bike Rental covers Locorotondo, Alberobello and Cisternino with delivery-to-accommodation. Indicative rates: €25–€35/day for an aluminium road or gravel bike, €45–€60/day carbon, €35–€45/day e-bike; weekly €190–€260. One-way drop-off in Lecce is possible with most operators for a €50–€80 repositioning fee — agree it in writing at booking. Bike boxes are stored free by Puglia On Bike for the rental duration.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation logistics: Sotto le Cummerse in Locorotondo distributes guests across restored houses and locks bikes in a ground-floor annexe; Masseria Salamina at Pezze di Greco has a stone outbuilding, a hose and a compressor line; Masseria Il Frantoio near Ostuni will store bikes in the old olive mill. Ask specifically for a room at ground level — Valle d'Itria stairs are stone, narrow and unforgiving with a bike on your shoulder.
raw.Bike on public transport: Trenitalia regional services take bikes on a €3.50 ticket valid 24 hours, in marked carriages. The Ferrovie del Sud Est network — Bari–Putignano–Martina Franca–Taranto and the Lecce branches — carries bikes on regional trains with a supplement but has limited space and no reservation, and replacement buses will not take them. Check FSE engineering works before relying on the Martina Franca line.

sources.confidenceNotes: All rental day and weekly rates are indicative and should be re-checked against 2026 price lists, as should the one-way Lecce drop-off fee and free bike-box storage. FSE bike-carriage rules and current engineering works must be confirmed close to travel — this is the most volatile fact in the file. Egnazia and Torre Guaceto entry prices and Torre Guaceto's guided-access requirements change season to season. Restaurant names in Cisternino's fornello scene turn over faster than most of Puglia; verify Zio Pietro is still trading. Masseria Il Frantoio and Palazzo Rollo rates are prior-season estimates.
